The primary captured rows publish an explicit harness for every one of these nine observations, e.g. SOURCE 1 (row 1, anthropic/claude-opus-5-5) "harness":"OpenHands"; SOURCE 4 (row 5, openai/gpt-6-sol) "harness":"OpenHands"; SOURCE 5 (row 6, grok/grok-4.7) "harness":"OpenHands"; SOURCE 6 (row 8, xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro) "harness":"OpenHands"; SOURCE 7 (row 14, openai/gpt-6-luna) "harness":"OpenHands"; SOURCE 8 (row 18, xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-flash) "harness":"OpenHands"; SOURCE 9 (row 20, zai/glm-5.3) "harness":"OpenHands"; SOURCE 10 (row 47, zai/glm-5.3-flash) "harness":"OpenHands"; SOURCE 11 (row 60, ant/ling-3.0-flash-af-rc3) "harness":"OpenHands". Every candidate row instead emits subject.harness=null and its protocol string documents only "its published compute/reasoning effort", so the harness field is recorded as unknown although the mapped source rows state it explicitly (the emitted per-row context projection is limited to context_keys and therefore silently drops the harness field present in each source_row). This leaves the row-level identity/configuration record for c1 incomplete on an explicitly published field, and cannot support any later harness-sensitive comparison, while comparison_key is emitted as null for the one row whose model/checkpoint is resolved (public:8b4a17b4f6b4cb6617302029, model_id glm-5.3::max).
